guia.what: Picks one of a few mutually exclusive options. It’s a radiogroup—you move through it with the arrow keys (selection follows focus), and it exposes its value. A good fit for switching views or filters where a Select would be overkill.
whenUse: Switching between 2–4 options that should always be visible (views, filters).
The change shows up instantly, and opening a panel isn’t worth it.
You want the options and the selected one to read at a glance.
whenAvoid: There are many options, or they don’t fit → `select`.
The options need a description or stack vertically → `radio`.
It’s navigation between content sections, not a value → `tabs`.
dos: Keep labels short and similar in length, so they fit the same width without wrapping.
A handful of options at most. If you’re unsure, it’s already a `select`.
donts: Don’t use it to move between pages or large views → `tabs`.
Don’t cram in six options. It gets tight and loses legibility.

teclado.action: Next and previous segment (wrapping around). On an RTL page they swap: ← moves forward and → moves back.
Next and previous segment, like a native radio group. They don’t depend on the writing direction.

nucleo: Core owns the selection and keyboard navigation between segments. Selects the segment, keeps `aria-checked` in sync, and moves between options with the arrow keys.
